argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification at the overall release level because aggregate launch readiness clears threshold by 2.5 percentage points, the launch rehearsal shows no severity-one incidents, and public AI-governance guidance permits deployment with documented limitations and ongoing monitoring. The narrower point is that the same record does not strongly support omitting a material weakness disclosure for the developer-support migration segment. A supportable audit position is therefore that certification is defensible only in a caveated sense: the model can be certified on overall readiness, while the basis for no disclosure remains weak on the present record.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the partner launch path. That cost is real, but it is not itself a policy defense. It supports avoiding unnecessary escalation if the auditor can distinguish overall certification support from the weaker no-disclosure position and reflect that distinction through a caveat rather than a full noncompliance finding.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not make aggregate readiness or low projected volume dispositive on materiality. The admissible policy text says a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case, and product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending. On this record, the named-segment evidence and open legal review prevent a clean claim that omission of disclosure is policy-compliant. The most defensible policy reading is caveated compliance for certification overall, not a clean compliance finding for certification without disclosure.
concessions: No new evidence is available to show the gap was resolved before launch.
No new evidence is available to show an approved risk acceptance covering launch without disclosure.
The 7% projected first-month traffic characterization does not, by itself, defeat materiality under the stated policy.
The present record is materially stronger for certification in general than for omission of a material weakness disclosure.
